verdict.rationale: Firecrawl documents server-side scoping of an individual API key to specific endpoints and output formats, which requests cannot override. It also documents IP/CIDR allowlists for a team's API keys, giving real least-privilege controls. However, the evidence never documents the workflow for issuing separate, dedicated keys to an agent, and the scoping depth is limited to endpoints, formats and network origin. missing for 10: documented per-agent key issuance/management workflow, key expiry/rotation or revocation controls, finer-grained permission scopes beyond endpoints/formats, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Lock an individual API key to specific output formats and endpoints. Enforced server-side, with no way for a request to override it.
Restrict your team's API keys to an allowlist of IP addresses or CIDR ranges, so they only work from approved networks. Enforced server-side.
